text: Three bytes per pixel gives about 16.7 million colours. Why is three enough?
choices: Because screens have three physical layers
Human retinas have three cone types, so three numbers reproduce a colour for a human observer
Because 256 cubed is the largest convenient number
Because light contains exactly three wavelengths
explanation: Two physically different spectra producing the same three cone responses look identical — they are metamers. The encoding is a choice about the observer, which is why scientific instruments use dozens of channels rather than three.
